steps.title: Copper colour
steps.body: Ramato means copper-coloured in Italian. It's a traditional style of Pinot Grigio from Friuli and Veneto, made with skin contact. Because Pinot Gris has pink-grey skins, leaving the juice on them for hours or days gives a copper or salmon hue, plus more body, texture and flavour.

steps.title: A Venetian tradition
steps.body: Ramato was traditional in the Republic of Venice, where Pinot Grigio was made this way. Modern, pale Pinot Grigio, pressed quickly, became popular from the 1960s. Since the 2000s, producers have revived ramato, sometimes with longer skin contact, linking it to the orange wine movement.

steps.prompt: Why does ramato have a copper colour?
options: Skin contact with Pinot Gris' pink-grey skins
steps.explanation: The skins' pigment tints the juice.

steps.title: Taste
steps.body: Ramato is fuller and more textured than standard Pinot Grigio, with red apple, peach, dried herbs, and a light tannic grip. It's dry, and works well with food. Its colour sits between rosé and orange wine.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Ramato is copper-coloured Pinot Grigio made with skin contact
It's a Venetian tradition revived since the 2000s
It's fuller and more textured than standard Pinot Grigio
